_what: Strong Workforce / Centers of Excellence region for every California Community College, derived from college_geo's county column.
_why: Sam, 2026-09-16: 'You should have the SW region in our dataset from MAP--check it.' He was right. college_geo carries a COUNTY per college, and the SWP consortia are defined by county, so the mapping is derivable rather than missing.
_derivation: college_geo.region is a nine-way grouping that agrees with the nine SWP regions on SEVEN of nine exactly, by county. Two differ, and only three colleges move.
_corroboration: Bay Area resolved to 28 colleges across 12 counties, matching the Bay Region COE's own published description of itself. The county derivation and the COE's self-description are independent, and they agree.
_status: APPLIED 2026-09-16 to map_colleges.swp_region + swp_region_code via migration add_swp_region_to_map_colleges. 117 of 118 college and continuing-education rows carry a region. The one exception is Calbright College Non-Credit, which is statewide and online and belongs to no regional consortium. Reversible: alter table map_colleges drop column swp_region, drop column swp_region_code — every pre-existing value was null, so the rollback is total.

renames._note: Same colleges, the consortium's own name.

moves._note: SWP puts Monterey, Santa Cruz and San Benito counties in the BAY region. college_geo has them under Central Coast. These three colleges move; nothing else does.

_counties_are_the_key: Assign region by COUNTY, never by name similarity. The county column is what makes this checkable, and it is why the two mismatches were findable at all.
_next: Confirm with Sam, then add swp_region + swp_region_code to the college taxonomy alongside district and mis_district_code, and flip the SWP scope to ready:true in college_briefing.js. The ASCCC area (four areas, A-D) is a SEPARATE scheme and stays disabled.
